revisions.title: Night Earth · Dark — centered
revisions.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit this Atlas desktop UI concept, preserving the reference's quiet Apple-inspired near-black interface, opaque charcoal panel material, off-white system typography, subtle blue atmosphere, small ATLAS wordmark and minimal bottom-center Search / News dock. Make one beautiful production-quality landscape image, same aspect ratio as reference. This is one screenshot concept, no device frame or collage.

PRIMARY CORRECTION — EXACT VIEWPORT CENTER AND COMPLETE SPHERE:
Shrink and reposition Earth so its center is EXACTLY the center of the entire canvas (50% width, 50% height), not centered in the space to the left of the panel. The sphere's diameter is 72% of the canvas height. The full circular silhouette AND its atmospheric rim must be visible with generous uninterrupted black margin on every side, at least 13% of image height at the top and bottom. No cropping, no touching edges, no hidden arc behind the panel. Globe rightmost edge approximately 72.5% of canvas width for this 16:10 landscape. Do not enlarge Earth to fill empty left space. Place the floating panel between x=76% and 98% so it does not obscure any part of Earth. The composition should feel like a perfectly centered whole planet floating in generous black negative space, with a slim independent reading panel at the far right. Keep the sphere fully visible even though the panel is open. Keep small dock BELOW the sphere, with clear gap.

PANEL CONTENT CORRECTION — REAL ARTICLE DATA:
Replace the sparse generic Hurricane Helene card with a compact but information-rich article detail panel, opaque near-black with subtle hairline border, 22px equivalent rounded corners, careful spacing, no excessive buttons. Panel around 22% screen width, y=9% to 88%. Do not widen panel or shift Earth to make room. Use thoughtfully nested text sizes and fine dividers, not a stack of cards.
Render this exact hierarchy and text:
Header: small left chevron and "Article"; simple close × on right.
Eyebrow: "HISTORICAL COVERAGE · 2024"
Headline, prominent but comfortably fitting in 2–3 lines: "Flash Floods Swamp North Carolina"
Publisher: "NASA Earth Observatory"
Metadata, muted: "Published 05 Oct 2024 · 16:00 UTC"
Fine divider.
Small location label: "LOCATION"
Value: "Asheville · Buncombe County"
Small muted line: "Regional coverage"
Topic labels in quiet unboxed text: "Flooding · Hurricanes · Drinking water"
Small contextual paragraph: "Historical reporting linked to Asheville and Buncombe County."
Quiet text link: "Read original article ↗"
Fine divider.
Small heading: "Related reporting"
Related row 1: publisher "USGS · 04 Oct 2024", title "USGS is collecting flood data and repairing streamgages damaged by Hurricane Helene"
Related row 2: publisher "WLOS · 12 Oct 2024", title "Buncombe County sees first water flow since Hurricane Helene"
Footer: "Curated historical sources"
These article headlines, publishers and dates come from existing Atlas historical source records; do not add invented statistics, author names, quotes, live badges or article thumbnails. Use crisp readable typography and appropriately compact typesetting. Related headlines may wrap. Keep quiet top-to-bottom reading hierarchy, panel contents fully inside the panel with comfortable padding.

Keep original ATLAS wordmark top left, bottom center tiny Search / News capsule with News selected, one discreet layers control bottom left, "Design concept" bottom right. Do not add top navigation, sidebars, multiple panels, charts, extra buttons, particles, unrelated ornaments or decorative grids. Refine polish while preserving reference identity.
EARTH IDENTITY: preserve the reference's night Earth: dark land, almost-black oceans, detailed warm city lights, subtle relief, thin cool blue atmospheric rim, North America facing forward. Maintain realistic city lights and geography at the reduced size. Keep enough shading to see a round globe. No daytime Earth or added clouds hiding city lights.

framingCorrection.prompt:
Precise layout correction to this image. KEEP ALL EXISTING UI, ARTICLE TEXT, PANEL, WORDMARK, DOCK, STARS, GEOGRAPHY, COLORS, MATERIALS AND LIGHTING IDENTICAL. Change ONLY the globe's position and very slightly its size if needed.

The globe is currently too far left. Move the globe to the RIGHT so its geometric center is exactly at the midpoint of the FULL IMAGE, including the panel area. Do not center it in the area left of the article panel. The Search/News dock is already centered in the full image: the center of Earth must align EXACTLY vertically above the CENTER OF THAT DOCK. Draw an imaginary straight vertical line through the dock's center; Earth must have equal width on BOTH sides of that line.

For this 1586x992 reference, globe center must be pixel (793,496). Target spherical radius 370 pixels; left edge x=423, right edge x=1163, top edge y=126, bottom edge y=866. All four limb extremes and blue atmosphere must be visible. This leaves a clear dark gap between globe right edge and the unchanged article panel left edge near x=1192. DO NOT move the panel. DO NOT move or change the dock. DO NOT enlarge Earth. DO NOT add a guide line, labels, coordinates or annotations. Preserve all text verbatim, no new content. A single polished desktop app screenshot with a truly centered complete planet and the existing slim right-hand dark article panel.
